body_text:
The Sequential Criterion for Limits and Continuity. Let
$f : U \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $x_0$ be an accumulation point of
$U$. Then $\lim_{x \to x_0} f(x) = L$ if and only if for every
sequence $(x_n)$ in $U \setminus \{x_0\}$ converging to $x_0$, the
sequence of outputs satisfies $f(x_n) \to L$.

Consequently, $f$ is continuous at $x_0$ if and only if
$f(\lim x_n) = \lim f(x_n)$ for every sequence converging to
$x_0$. This criterion provides the operational bridge converting
continuous analytical assertions into discrete sequence problems.
